retained_measurement.verdict: FAIL_STRICT_ONE_SECOND_OBSERVATION; consistent with periodic CPU termination, not proof of exact detection latency

semantics.finding: Job user-time threshold is checked periodically after accumulated user time exceeds it. No numerical maximum checking interval is specified. Existing accumulated time is added when setting the limit; the candidate sets it on a fresh empty Job before process creation, so that addition cannot justify this overrun.

TERMINATE ends the Job and prevents further assignment until reset. The source never resets it during a role. POST notification can clear a time limit and continue execution, so it is not an acceptable substitute.
External termination is asynchronous; wait on retained process handles for actual exit. Pending IO can delay final process exit. A stop request or wait timeout is not a completed-closure proof.

TotalUserTime and TotalKernelTime include terminated Job processes. Nested root/private accounting overlaps and must not be added as disjoint work. TotalProcesses is not a unique successful-birth inventory.

HARD_CAP controls CPU cycles per scheduling interval, not an absolute lifetime user-time budget. No numeric interval/phase or cycles-to-user-time bound is supplied here. This mechanism is not configured in the reviewed candidate.

existing_mechanism_decision.missing: Scheduling, blocking-call and last-process-stop latency bound. Native threads remove Python/GIL dependence but do not supply hard-real-time scheduling.

existing_mechanism_decision.missing: An observed maximum does not establish worst-case latency; no invented safety margin is permitted.
